record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a triangle-free graph on n vertices. Can G always be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2/25 edges?

evidence.quote: Mentioning the bipartitions of triangle-free graphs, a long-standing conjecture of Erd˝os (see [10, p. 363] or [25]) is still open.

Conjecture 1.1 (Erd˝os’ Conjecture) Every triangle-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most n2
25 edges.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A graph is called triangle-free if it contains no three pairwise adjacent vertices, and bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two parts so that every edge has its endpoints in different parts. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every triangle-free graph G on n vertices, there exists a set of at most n^2/25 edges whose removal from G yields a bipartite graph.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture of Erdős that every triangle-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most n^2/25 edges remains open. The best known general upper bound has been improved to about n^2/23.5 (from an earlier n^2/18), and the conjecture has been verified in certain edge-density regimes (e.g., density at most about 0.2486 and at least about 0.3197), but no full proof or disproof is known.

status_evidence.title: Making a triangle-free graph bipartite (Erdős problems)
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős conjectured every triangle-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most n^2/25 edges; listed as an open Erdős problem.

status_evidence.title: Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs (arXiv:2103.14179)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves bounds toward Erdős's n^2/25 conjecture, establishing it for new ranges of edge density and improving the absolute bound to roughly n^2/23.5.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress; full conjecture not yet proven.

status_evidence.title: 10 problems for partitions of triangle-free graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists Erdős's n^2/25 bipartization conjecture among current open problems on partitions of triangle-free graphs.
